the model says the meaning changed: The change drops the exemption for dispatch failures (no judge to ask), so a job failing three times because the judge is unreachable can now open a debug case, while SR-245 only has such records wait with one line, and EX-11 sends a case to debugging only after out-of-schema answers that were retried.; filed as a question for the owner, to ask with the question tool: The requirement still matches what you asked for. When no judge can be reached, plumb says so once, applies the verdicts it already has, and holds only the records that still need a verdict. A broken judge answer that was already retried counts as a case to debug (EX-11). A judge that simply can't be reached is not plumb's fault. The old code reflected this: it never opened a debug case when there was no model to ask, because a bigger budget can't fix a missing key or a service that is down.

The change does two things. It counts failures for each job on its own, which seems to be the point. It also drops that exception. So now a job that fails three times in a row because the judge is unreachable opens a debug case and adds output beyond the single waiting line.

No example says outright that this must never happen, and the prompt for that turn is empty. It's unclear whether dropping the exception was intended or a side effect of moving to per-job counting.; the card is not offered until it is complete, it lacks: what option 1 ("Put the exception back: an unreachable judge never opens a debug case, and failures are still counted per job") does and leaves undone; what option 2 ("Keep the change: three unreachable-judge failures in a row on the same job open a debug case, and the requirement is reworded to say so") does and leaves undone; what option 3 ("Open a debug case for an unreachable judge only when the setup is plainly wrong (for example, no judge configured), not for timeouts or outages") does and leaves undone; why the recommended option is recommended (plumb stale card SR-245#14 --consequences "..." --why "...")
